The Pacific Northwest Traffic League generally supports the proposal but urges that the Seattle zone be further expanded to include certain suburban areas around Tacoma which do not fall within the proposed new zone. Finally, the Indiana Port Commission argues that the population-mileage formula should be amended by adding a category for cities with populations of 2 million or more in order to differentiate between large cities such as Houston and New York. It also notes that three of the cities with populations of one million or more (New York, Los Angeles, and Chicago) are built adjacent to bodies of water and, therefore, have not developed concentrically. It urges that these cities be given a radius of 30 miles from their corporate limits.
Shipping interests in several cities seek various exemptions from the proposed regulations for their cities. Interests in Miami seek to have it exempted from the consolidated governments rule and to have Broward County as well as Dade County included in the Miami zone. In support of this they point to the migration of population and industry from Dade County to Broward County in recent years.
Several shipper interests urge that various cities be treated as twin cities. These cities are San Francisco and Oakland, Calif., Cincinnati, Ohio and Covington and Newport, Ky., and Tampa and St. Petersburg, Fla.
